key_insight: The paper extends stochastic fluid thermodynamics to compressible, variable-density flows by making mass, momentum, and energy source-consistent while enforcing entropy admissibility with finite-correlation stochastic reservoirs.
engineering_relevance: It offers a thermodynamically consistent framework for modeling compressible turbulent flows, pressure fluctuations, and low-Mach limits in CFD and turbulence closures.
method: Separates stochastic transport into PDE evolution laws plus martingale compatibility constraints.
Uses resolved kinetic-energy balance with a finite-correlation reservoir, Green–Kubo calibration, and an adjoint exchange term.
Derives a stochastic Gibbs identity and Gaussian relative entropy condition for admissible entropy production.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports canonical calculations that verify the pressure carrier, acoustic dispersion, viscous-thermal energy balance, and low-Mach scaling.
watch_item: Nonlinear well-posedness, shock admissibility, and fully developed turbulence are not established, so practical deployment still needs stability and validation work.
paper_title: Compressible solved-volatility stochastic fluid thermodynamics: source-consistent energy, finite-correlation reservoirs, entropy admissibility and boundary conditions
